author: Aeliren
content:
Leaving this here, but right now this is a list of things the wiki needs help with:

— Someone skilled with wikia/fandom source coding to replicate Wowpedia’s style and adapt it properly to the Turtle WoW wiki. Right now it’s very messily done, several things are coded manually on each page rather than neatly having templates to work from; this can be seen mainly in the faction reaction tags, which are individually coded in the correct color for friendly, hostile, etc. rather than a clean {{Aggro|1|-1}} template. — Help for adding Horde-side content in particular: quests, zones, NPCs, gossip text, etc. I personally have no high level Horde characters so I can’t really check it all out myself.
— Help transferring over already-existing Classic content from wowpedia. This is mostly to conserve cohesiveness on the wiki concerning content, as some original zones and NPCs have new content attached to them. It’d be a bit annoying to have a hyperlink from Hawk’s Vigil going to the wowpedia page for classic Wetlands and no return link, for example. Generally speaking this will primarily be a copy-and-paste job and adapting it as needed in regards to content as present in Turtle WoW.
— Other Turtle WoW-exclusive content is missing from the wiki; items, NPCs, quests of all levels, even on Alliance-side.

author: Jortii
content:
# __**New Horde Quest Hubs**__

__Sparkwater Port:__ New town in Durotar.  Quests for all levels, check back occasionally. (This is where to pick up the new horde quests for Deadmines/Gnomer)

__Tirisfal Uplands:__ Quests for levels **14-20.**  Northwestern Tirisfal.

__Amani'Alor:__ Short intro questline leads to daily quests for Revantusk rep.  Can start grinding at lvl **12.**  Northwest of Stonetalon Mtns (Can teleport from Orgrimmar mage trainer)

__Powder Town:__ Quests for **22-27.** Western Stonetalon Mountains. 

__Wildtusk Village:__ Quests for level **35-40.**  North of Refuge Point (Arathi Highlands).  A hidden path leads up to it in the mountains and connects to Hinterlands.

__Mudsprocket:__ Quests for level **37-41.**  Southern Dustwallow Marsh.

__South Sea Enclave:__ Quests for level **37-45.**  On the coast of Jaguero Isle (south east STV)

__Gilneas:__ Quests for level **39 to 45.**  South of Silverpine Forest.

__Bloodfist Point:__ Quests for level **47-52.**  Northern cliffs of Azshara.

__Gillijim Isle & Island of Lapidis:__ Quests for level **50-52**  (Can fly there from Booty Bay)

__Tel'Abim Isle:__ Quests for level **54-60** (Can fly there from Gadgetzan)

__Mount Hyjal:__ Quests for level **58-60.**  Accessed thru Darkwhisper Gorge (Southern Winterspring)

Additionally, **many** quest hubs have been expanded but are not listed here because they are already on the traditional leveling path.

author: Matttt
content:
Gonna add this to discord just because people often search discord for quest issues before checking elsewhere. 
For the Alliance "Suspicous Hoofprints" quest chain in Dustwallow Marsh / Theramore there is a stumbling point where the database indicates that there is a single pre-requisite quest for the 2nd quest "Report From Falgran". However, there are in fact 3 pre-requisite quests, the other 2 being the followup quests from the badge and the shield portions of the Shady Rest Inn quests.
This is just how official databases report this quest, so the database is in fact working as intended. It's just a rare case in classic wow's quest system. 
For more information see this issue on the quest bug tracker and the forum post linked within. https://github.com/slowtorta/turtlewow-bug-tracker/issues/4045

- Naxxramas(Naxx)
- Emerald Sanctum(ES)

author: !!!𝗥𝗘𝗧𝗥𝗢🏹
content:
76-150 automatically unlocks. Not sure the exact level, I believe it's at 75, but it's automatic. You get a guaranteed 1 skill point in Survival every time you make a Bright Campfire all the way up to 150 skill (he highest you can get in Survival).

It requires Flint and Tinder (not consumed) and 1× Simple Wood (consumed) just like a regular Basic Campfire. It has a 5-minute cooldown (shared with Basic Campfire). You can use either fire for Cooking. The only difference is the Bright Campfire giving +8 spirit to nearby players, while Basic Campfire gives +4 spirit. Sadly the "Bright" one is visually the exact same as the "Basic" one.

I kept the required materials in my bags at all times (takes 2 slots and Simple Wood stacks to 20), put Bright Campfire on an action bar, and hit it whenever it was convenient and off cooldown.

By far the easiest and cheapest way to hit 150, although certainly not the quickest.
